name: Pohlman, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Condemarin's holding is limited and does not control the constitutionality of the 2017 GIA's damages cap because the statutes are different and Condemarin lacked a majority rationale.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Recused, did not participate in the decision.

name: Associate Chief Justice Pearce
description: Recused, did not participate in the decision.

name: ASSOCIATE CHIEF JUSTICE PEARCE
description: Concurred, arguing that the court clarified the Brickey standard to prevent prosecutorial bad faith or harassment while allowing the State to refile charges under specific conditions, and that the Victims' Rights Amendment abrogated the discovery purpose of preliminary hearings.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE DURRANT
description: Concurred, argued that subsections (2)(b) and the waiver component of (2)(c) of the Plea Withdrawal Statute are unconstitutional as they violate the separation of powers by being procedural rules enacted by the legislature.

name: ASSOCIATE CHIEF JUSTICE PEARCE
description: Recused himself and did not participate.

name: JUSTICE HAGEN
description: Concurred, argued that the Legislature failed to follow constitutional requirements for submitting and publishing Amendment D, rendering it void.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred, argued that Baugh's counsel was objectively unreasonable for failing to request specific unanimity instructions, leading to a significant risk of a non-unanimous verdict and prejudice.

name: DURRANT, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that property used to generate profit, even if supporting a charitable mission, is not exclusively charitable, and future intent for vacant property does not qualify for a present exemption.

name: JUSTICE POHLMAN
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, finding that Bingham did not show the statute of repose violated constitutional provisions, and affirmed the district court's dismissal.

name: Justice Hagen
description: Concurred, authored the opinion affirming the Commission's decision, finding that the County failed to show the Aircraft Valuation Law was unconstitutional as applied or on its face.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred, arguing that Kell's five-year delay in filing his petition, after discovering new evidence, was not excused by ineffective assistance of prior counsel and did not violate his constitutional rights under the PCRA's time and procedural bars.

name: Justice Lee
description: Did not participate in the consideration of the case.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Did not participate in the consideration of the case.

name: Associate Chief Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the Utah Constitution's Bail Provision does not mandate denial of bail for certain defendants but allows judges discretion to grant it, based on plain language and the 1988 voters' understanding.

name: The Court
description: Concurred, holding that petitioners failed to demonstrate that a school district's tax increase is subject to a referendum under the Utah Constitution or relevant statutes.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, argued that improper jury contacts by authoritative figures trigger a rebuttable presumption of prejudice, requiring the State to prove harmlessness beyond a reasonable doubt.

name: Justice Petersen
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's balancing test for prejudice is novel and distorts existing precedent, and that the district court's handling of the matter already satisfied the standard.

name: Lee, Associate Chief Justice
description: Concurred, authored the opinion of the Court, affirming the dismissal of zoning challenges and declining to rule on tax provisions due to mootness.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Authored the majority opinion, concluding Laws lacked standing to challenge Grayeyes's election and affirming the denial of attorney fees to Grayeyes.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Laws lacked standing due to not identifying a private injury and that Grayeyes was not entitled to attorney fees under the private attorney general doctrine.

name: Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that the Utah Constitution's standing requirements should be re-examined, questioning the reliance on federal precedents and inconsistencies in state jurisprudence.

name: Justice Pearce
description: Concurred, argued that most of Patterson's claims were time-barred under the PCRA, but two claims based on newly discovered evidence should be remanded.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Concurred, argued that Patterson's claims were time-barred and no egregious injustice exception applied, but parts of the majority's constitutional analysis were premature and unnecessary.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, argued that individuals have a common-law right to change their sex designation and courts have the authority to adjudicate such petitions, reversing the district court's denial.

name: Chief Justice Durrant
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, arguing that the legislature intended name and sex changes to be treated uniformly under a 'proper cause' standard, but disagreed with the majority's specific two-part test.

name: Associate Chief Justice Lee
description: Dissented, arguing the court overstepped its judicial power by creating new law on sex designation and infringing on democratic norms.

name: Justice Himonas
description: Concurred, arguing that while the Limitations on Landowner Liability Act can bar wrongful death claims and is constitutional, the plaintiffs sufficiently alleged that the death was not caused by an inherent risk, thus reversing the dismissal and remanding the case.
